UNH.rationale: UNH is a dominant franchise (largest US healthcare company by revenue, ~$447B TTM) with a strong integrated model (UnitedHealthcare + Optum) and massive scale advantages. However, the company has been through a severe operational reset: 2025 saw earnings misses, guidance cuts, leadership transitions (Witty departure, Hemsley return), the Change Healthcare cyberattack fallout, and a DOJ probe into Optum Rx. The Q1 2026 results show a clear inflection: adjusted EPS of $7.23 beat consensus of $6.58, medical care ratio improved to 83.9% (vs 84.8% YoY, well below the 85.5% consensus), and full-year guidance was raised to >$18.25 adjusted EPS from >$17.75. Revenue grew 2% YoY to $111.7B. Operating cash flow was strong at $8.9B (1.4x net income), and the company initiated $B..7;s debt-to-capital ratio to initiated $2B in accelerated buybacks. Valuation is attractive: at $354.56, the stock trades at 17.5x trailing PE, which is below the midpoint of its 9.5-26.1x range over the past year and well below the ~26x level from April 2025. P/B of 3.17x is also below the 4.0x peak. The stock is ~17% below its 252-week high of $429.90. However, significant risks remain: medical cost trends are still elevated, Medicare Advantage enrollment declined 965K in Q1, Optum Rx scripts fell, and the DOJ probe is unresolved. The Q1 beat is encouraging but one quarter does not constitute a durable trend. The near-term catalyst (Q1 earnings beat + guidance raise) has already been priced in with the stock up ~8.5% on the day. Net margin at 4.2% and ROE at 18.1% are below historical norms, suggesting the earnings power recovery is still early. Score reflects a solid franchise at a reasonable valuation with a positive inflection, but tempered by execution risks and the need for multiple quarters of proof.

sources_cited.excerpt: UnitedHealth Group reported first-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $7.23, beating consensus estimates of $6.58, with revenues of $111.721 billion. The company raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings per share guidance to more than $18.25 from over $17.75. Medical cost ratios improved significantly, declining 90 basis points year-over-year to 83.9%.

UnitedHealth Group (UNH) shares surged 8.51% after delivering a strong Q1 earnings beat with adjusted EPS of $7.23 versus consensus of $6.58, and revenue of $111.7 billion. The company raised its full-year 2026 EPS guidance to greater than $18.25 from $17.75.

UnitedHealth's medical benefit ratio came in at 83.9% for the first quarter. That's an improvement from the 84.8% reported in the year-earlier period. A lower ratio typically indicates that the company collected more in premiums than it paid out in benefits, resulting in higher profitability. Analysts were expecting a ratio of 85.5% for the quarter

Operating cash flows from operations were $8.9 billion, or 1.4 times net income, and the debt-to-capital ratio was 42.9% as of March 31, 2026. We initiated share repurchases earlier than anticipated and expect to deploy at least $2 billion by the end of the second quarter.
Seniors served through Medicare Advantage declined by 965,000 in the first quarter 2026.
Optum Rx's first quarter 2026 revenues of $35.7 billion increased 2% year-over-year. Adjusted scripts were 383 million compared to 408 million last year.
UNH's Optum segment faces operational and regulatory headwinds, including margin erosion in value-based care and an expanding DOJ probe into Optum Rx
